scope: Menteşe southwest coast: Datça, Bozburun, Marmaris, Köyceğiz/Dalaman, Fethiye/Meğri
method: Political control is separated from settlement, port, route, and later administrative boundaries.
Later 14th-century or Ottoman evidence is not back-projected as 1326 polygon evidence.
Where evidence supports regional Menteşe presence but not an exact 1326 frontier, retain an anchor/frontier classification rather than inventing a boundary.

anchors.name: Datça peninsula / Dadya
anchors.evidence: A historical study of Knidos/Datça states that by 1269 the Karia/Trachia/Stadia area had passed to Turkish groups and describes the peninsula as under Menteşe control, with an inland local administrative center at Batır/Hızırşah. Medieval settlement was dispersed and shifted inland for security.
anchors.guard: Do not convert the whole peninsula into a precise 1326 political polygon solely from later administrative geography.

anchors.name: Hızırşah / Batır
anchors.evidence: The Datça historical study identifies an inland Menteşe administrative center at Batır/Hızırşah; the surviving Hızırşah mosque is generally dated to the Menteşe period, but its exact construction date and the identity of Hızırşah are disputed.
anchors.guard: Treat the settlement as an anchor, not proof of a modern-style district boundary.

anchors.name: Marmaris / Physkos
anchors.evidence: Marmaris municipal historical chronology places the area in the Menteşe period from around 1290 and describes Marmaris as a large port settlement in the 1300s. Later scholarship records Marmaris as part of Menteşe territory.
anchors.guard: The surviving Marmaris castle is Ottoman-period (1522); do not use that fortress as a 1326 fortification.

anchors.name: Köyceğiz / Kaunos area
anchors.evidence: Muğla Provincial Government describes Kaunos/Köyceğiz as an important ancient port and states that the area was conquered by Menteşeoğulları in 1291. TDV's Menteşe overview includes Köyceğiz among the later-attested Menteşe cities/areas.
anchors.guard: The modern Köyceğiz settlement is not a 1326 polygon. Model the Kaunos/lake/coastal corridor as historical landscape and regional anchor until stronger contemporary evidence is found.

anchors.name: Dalaman valley / Dalaman Çayı
anchors.evidence: Menteşe sources describe the broader southwest as the beylik's territory, while historical-geographical material places Dalaman within the later Menteşe region. The available evidence does not establish a precise 7 April 1326 political line at the Dalaman river.
anchors.guard: Keep as frontier/transition terrain rather than a hard political border.

anchors.name: Fethiye / Meğri / Makri
anchors.evidence: TDV describes Meğri/Fethiye as a Menteşe port city and records Menteşe architectural activity there. A Menteşe Bey tomb is located at Fethiye, although its surviving structure was renovated/rebuilt later. Later Menteşe political organization explicitly places southern coastal control around Fethiye and Marmaris.
anchors.guard: Do not date Ahmed Gazi's later 1360–1391 southern division back to 1326; use it only as corroboration of the established southern Menteşe zone.

anchors.name: Eşen valley / northern Lycian transition
anchors.evidence: Menteşe regional sources include Meğri and its hinterland, while the southern/eastern boundary toward Teke is not sufficiently resolved for a 1326 polygon from the sources reviewed here.
anchors.guard: Do not assign the whole Eşen basin to Menteşe or Teke without date-specific evidence.

negativeControls.reason: The extant major castle is associated with Süleyman's 1522 Rhodes campaign; it is not evidence for a 1326 fortress.
The documented Fethiye/Marmaris southern branch belongs to the post-1360 political division and must not be projected to 1326 as an administrative subdivision.

runtimeImplications: Represent Datça, Marmaris, Köyceğiz/Kaunos and Meğri/Fethiye as settlement/port/route anchors with historical control metadata.
Use a broad Menteşe regional control layer where evidence is strong, but keep exact frontier geometry unresolved.
Model the southwest coast as a maritime network: ports, anchorages, sea lanes and piracy exposure are more historically meaningful than a smooth coastal province polygon.
Keep the Dalaman–Eşen direction as a frontier review zone pending stronger date-specific evidence.
